title: Build a small Python interpreter in C with coding agents
summary: A developer spent about $500 having Codex and then Claude Code build a 25,000-line C version of Python 3.15 over three days, covering almost all language features.
agent_role: Codex built the first proof of concept; Claude Code did all later development in one long session. The human directed the project.
outcome: Author reports almost full Python 3.15 language features and built-in functions, without the standard library, for about $500.
what_they_did: The poster wanted a small, embeddable Python written in plain C. They started a prototype with Codex, restarting it three times. They then moved all development to one Claude Code session that ran over three days.
how_it_went: They say the result covers almost all Python 3.15 language features and built-ins in about 25,000 lines of C. It does not include Python's standard library.
worth_knowing: The author says the whole project cost about $500 in agent usage.
prompt: Build a small, embeddable interpreter for [language] in plain C, with no outside libraries. Start by writing a plan listing which language features and built-in functions you will cover, and show it to me before coding. Then work feature by feature, writing automatic tests for each one and running them as you go. Keep a progress file of what works and what is left. Stop and summarize after each major milestone so I can review.

curation.rationale: A concrete agent-built project with code and cost figures, but the post is brief on method and testing.
